messages:
Lena: Quick experiment log — spun up a split-queue run to isolate prefill vs decode batching for a 4k-context model. Wanted to see KV warmup impact on tail latency.
Rafael: Nice. Which metric are you watching? p95/p99 gen-latency or prefill completion time?
Lena: Mainly p99 end-to-end and decode-stage latency (post-prefill). Prefill time isn't super important except when it blocks infer hot paths.
Nguyen: Did you change the token budget targets or queue weights for the split?
Lena: Yes, I dropped prefill token_budget_target from 64->16 and bumped decode's min_batch_target to 8. The idea: keep prefill bursts short to avoid locking KV-heavy kernels.
Maria: Any kernel-selection changes? prefills hit matmul/kv-copy kernels more often.
Lena: No kernel binaries changed. I tweaked kernel_affinity hints in scheduler: prefer lightweight decode kernels on smaller batches, route large prefill batches to optimized matmul path.
Jim: Can you paste the config snippet? also, link to the perf dashboard.
Lena: Sure:

```
queue_policy {
  prefill {
    token_budget_target: 16
    max_batch_size: 128
    kernel_affinity: "matmul-heavy"
  }
  decode {
    token_budget_target: 48
    min_batch_target: 8
    kernel_affinity: "latency-optimized"
  }
}
```

Dash: https://perf.internal/redwood/exp/1865432109
OpsBot: Deploy started for branch split-queue/sched-tweaks @ 2026-02-11T15:22:05Z :rocket:
Rafael: Flamegraph looks weird — decode stage has extra syscalls around KV eviction. Could be our KV drain heuristic.
Lena: I saw that. When prefill batches are small, KV cache gets warmed but then decode threads trigger concurrent flushes. p99 spikes ~120ms -> 260ms in that bucket.
Nguyen: Is this reproducible locally with the microbenchmark? if so we can attach perf and eBPF.
Lena: Reproducible on staging. Ran `./bench/continuous_batcher --scenario split` and attached a perf report. Short summary:
- avg latency unchanged (~45ms)
- p95 decode up 10ms
- p99 decode up 140ms correlated with KV eviction bursts
Rafael: Proposed mitigation: add a KV-prefetch delay window for decode when prefill finished less than X ms ago, and increase prefill's token_budget slightly to reduce eviction churn.
Maria: That sounds plausible. Any risks? could increase prefill cost or push more load onto matmul kernel.
Lena: Tradeoff: +cost for fewer tail spikes. I tested token_budget prefill=24 with decode delay=30ms -> p99 drops back to ~110ms. Throughput impact negligible.
Jim: Can you add a simple flag behind an experiment gate so we can A/B? Also add a metric for KV-flush-count.
Lena: Yep, created PR: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/4521 (WIP). It wires queue flag `kv_prefetch_delay_ms` and exposes `kv_flush_count` in request traces.
OpsBot: CI passed for split-queue/sched-tweaks (tests: 12/12) :white_check_mark:
Rafael: Another angle — kernel selection: when prefill and decode are separate, our kernel selector sometimes picks a quantized matmul that has higher latency on small batch sizes. Maybe selector needs a batch-size-aware penalty.
Nguyen: Good call. We can add a small cost model: cost = kernel_base + alpha / batch_size. Prefer kernels with lower estimated cost for small batches.
Maria: alpha tuning will be key. Keep it conservative to avoid switching for stable large batches.
Lena: I'll prototype the cost-term and run a kernel-selection ablation. Plan:
1) Merge experiment gate for kv_prefetch_delay + metric
2) Add kernel-size penalty in selector behind feature flag
3) Run 24h A/B on beta region and collect p99/p95 + kv_flush_count
Rafael: If beta looks good, we can roll to dedicated and monitor rollback policies.
Jim: Thanks — please paste the beta run IDs here when started.
Lena: Started beta job 1865432710 — collecting traces. Will follow up with flamegraphs and a short runbook if we enable globally.
Nguyen: Great. If we see any regression, tag me and I'll dig into kernel traces with eBPF.
Lena: Thanks all. Next update in ~6h or earlier if we see regressions. :eyes:
